items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: Jordan was the man who drew it. He was a Belgian/painter

ctx.x: Yeah, and Jordan (PHONETIC), the Belgian painter (inaudible), Jordan was the man who drew it. He was a Belgian/painter, and it was beautiful. He said, I paid $200,000.00 for that, Jacques. And he had discoteques then. He had one looking like a freighter, a boat. And this ran night and day. He had 12 bartenders. Then he had another one, plush one, it ran night and day. And he says, now, we've got a thing called the Sugar Can, we can build that up again. If you come to Belgium, you've got it.

So we formed a company (inaudible). Now, I'm still working now, I'm still working at Cigale But I'm on vacation. (Inaudible). But these Americans, they're going to move in a year; they got mad and moved in a month. Pulled out, went to Belgium. Now, instead of them coming to Brussels, they went to a place called Helmut, means the helmet, about 18 miles from Brussels. Bad news. He had everything all set. And the Hilton Hotel thought that they was coming there, too. But the Hilton being rich, they could care less.
